newsitem.title: USA: Iraq to retender for 50,000 U.S. HRW wheat - trade.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to retender for 50,000 U.S. HRW wheat - trade.

text.p: Several U.S. exporters said Iraq may have passed offers from its original March 11 tender and will retender later this week for 50,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat.
"I don't think they bought," one U.S. exporter said.
A second U.S. exporter also said Iraq passed on Sunday night and will retender for 50,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat. "That's as far as I know," he said.
"To the best of my knowledge it is on March 21," a third U.S. exporter said of the re-tender date.
Delivery dates were slated for May 15-June 15.
Several exporters said they believed the wheat would be purchased under a United Nations-monitored oil-for-food deal.
The U.N. approved a recent sale of 100,000 tonnes of French wheat to Iraq under a U.N. pact, a French government source said on Monday.
The approval brings to 300,000 tonnes the volume of wheat which has been sold to Iraq and subsequently cleared by the U.N., the source said.

Although most exporters said they believed Iraq passed on the original tender Sunday, one U.S. exporter said he had heard that Iraq had bought 50,000 tonnes on Sunday but would re-tender for an additional 50,000 tonnes on Friday.
